title: Sprint-zero mentor notebook: compact SDK pilot
content:
Purpose: a very compact, mentor-focused Sprint‑Zero notebook to run a 1–3 day pilot for new internal teams adopting Redwood SDKs. Goal is a repeatable micro-workshop that leaves teams with a working sample, telemetry hooks, and a first small integration.

Audience: SDK mentors (internal devs, SEs), bootcamp leads, onboarding PMs. Not intended as end-user docs — this is the playbook mentors carry into pairing sessions and quick pilots.

High-level outcomes (1–3 days):
- Day 0 (prep): sandbox provisioned + seed repo forked
- Day 1 (hands-on): developer runs quickstart, sends first request, sees streaming + error path
- Day 2 (ops + telemetry): enable cheap KPIs, iterate prompt/params, failover test and handoff checklist completed

Recommended slate (condensed):
- Minimal app: single-page feedback widget that calls Redwood text generation, and a background embedding job for search. Keep UI trivial (textarea + result).
- Language/runtime: Node.js + fetch (polyglot patterns noted inline).
- Repo: seed/example-app with feature flags to switch between hosted and local-stub mode.

Micro-schedule (mentor script):
- 30m: Introductions + goals (explain latency vs cost tradeoffs).
- 60m: Clone repo, install, set API key, run local stub.
- 60m: Swap to hosted endpoint, run streaming demo, inspect token/latency metrics in console.
- 45m: Add simple prompt guard (system message template + max tokens), test edge case prompt that returns long output.
- 45m: Telemetry walk-through: add a single metric (request_time_ms) and a token counter; push and view in console.
- 30m: Failure rehearsal: simulate 429 and fallback to smaller model + user message explaining graceful degradation.
- 15m: Handoff: checklist, next steps, and owner assignment.

Quickstart checklist (what the mentor verifies):
- [ ] Repo cloned and dependency install succeeds
- [ ] API key loaded securely (env var or secret manager)
- [ ] Local stub mode reproduces shape of responses (use --stub flag)
- [ ] Hosted run returns streaming chunks and final JSON
- [ ] Telemetry events visible in console with request_time_ms and token_count
- [ ] Failover tested: simulated 429 triggers alternative model route
- [ ] Team has assigned follow-up owner and 3 next tickets

Sample minimal commands (for the mentor handout):
- Clone + run stub:
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/example-sdk-pilot.git
  cd example-sdk-pilot
  npm ci
  API_KEY=REDACTED npm run dev -- --stub

- Switch to hosted and run a streaming test (bash curl example):
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"Write a 3-line haiku about office coffee"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Telemetry gating and minimal instrumentation (opinions):
- Required: request_time_ms, token_count, http_status, model_name, route_used.
- Nice-to-have: prompt_version (string id), user_intent tag.
- Send events as batched logs to the Console ingest; sample SDK helper (one-liner) included in repo.
- Keep retention tiny during pilot (7 days) to avoid noise and cost.

Failover & graceful degradation patterns to demonstrate:
- Primary: rwd-medium (best quality)
- Fallback: rwd-small (faster, cheaper)
- Policy: on 429 or avg latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive requests, switch route for 5 minutes and attach telemetry tag "fallback_reason".
- UX: show a non-blocking banner: "Responses may be slightly summarized for speed — toggle full mode".

Prompt iteration micro-workflow (mentor guide):
- Create a 10-item prompt test harness in repo (prompt-cases.json).
- Run harness across model variants and capture token usage + quality tags (ok/needs-tweak).
- If quality drops when moving to a smaller quantized model, add guardrail: request fewer tokens with a concise candidate template.

Edge cases and traps (real notes from past pilots):
- Secret leakage: mentors saw devs paste API keys into error screenshots — insist on redaction and sample token.
- Stub divergence: local stub may not exercise streaming or tool-calling; call out explicit tests for that.
- Telemetry overwhelm: too many high-cardinality tags in first week. Start with the 5 required fields only.

Handoff checklist (final):
- [ ] Follow-up tickets created: telemetry, production rollout plan, prompt-regression test set
- [ ] Team Slack channel created and wired to console alerts (mute by default)
- [ ] Security review triage (if private keys or customer data required)
- [ ] Demo recording saved to drive + short README

Mentor tips and language snippets:
- Keep explanations concrete: "We care about tokens because that directly maps to cost; measure tokens per success-case." 
- Use the failover demo: simulate 429 locally by flipping an env var; show the UX banner switching to compact-mode.
- If the team is non-engineering heavy, focus Day 1 on the UI + sample responses and defer telemetry to Day 2.

Unresolved questions (to capture & iterate):
- What is the minimum set of QA prompts we standardize across pilots? (propose 8–12 distinct intents)
- Should mentors be given an ops playbook for Dedicated vs Hosted differences? (current demo only covers Hosted + stub)
- Metric thresholds for automatic model fallback: what percentile of latency should be used? (P95 vs P99?)

Follow-ups and next iterations (short roadmap):
- v0.2 (2 weeks): add a 1-click sandbox provisioner to spawn a sample project per team.
- v0.3 (1 month): include an optional private-deploy note with secure KMS instructions for pilot customers.
- v1.0 (quarter): formalize mentor certification and a mini-badge for internal SEs who run 5+ pilots.

Quick reference: relevant artifacts
- Seed repo: github.com/redwood-inference/example-sdk-pilot (branch: mentor-sprint-zero)
- Confluence primer: link above
- Jira epic: DEVX-1243

Notes to self: carry a printed small checklist, keep the demo deterministic (fixed random seed), and avoid showing internal quotas that confuse customers.
